description.narrative: Resilience evaluation analysis and learning (real 2) program to provide evidence and learning to inform design and implementation of usaid-funded resilience investments for the benefit of implementers and public good and b) continued support for the broader development community, including host governments. the specific activities are linked to: a) generation of key resilience evidence; b) continued thought leadership on resilience measurement and analysis in frontier areas; and c) collaboration, learning, and adapting to enhance implementation of resilience programming.

title.narrative: MERC Technical and Administrative Support Contract

description.narrative: The purpose of the MERC/CDR Technical and Administrative Support Program is to provide technical and administrative support for two international collaborative research programs, the U.S.-Israel Cooperative Development Research (CDR) Program and the Middle East Regional Cooperation (MERC) Program. Both CDR and MERC fund collaborative research grants to address development problems while helping to strengthen international scientific capacity. The overall goal of the MERC/CDR Technical and Administrative Support Program is to facilitate USAID's external peer review process while assisting in both the processing of large volumes of research proposals and oversight of ongoing activities. The following are the main objectives of this program: a. For the U.S. scientific community to provide voluntary advice and assistance to the MERC and CDR Programs through substantive peer-review panels evaluation of research proposals, individually and collectively. The products of the peer-review advice are to be used by USAID to assist the Agency in determining which proposals to select for award and what additional technical, administrative, regulatory and/or budgetary provisos to place on the projects before awards are made. b. To assist USAID in its monitoring of technical progress of grants funded under the MERC and CDR Programs by summarizing the grantees' scientific reports of progress and providing information in response to inquiries from USAID. This should facilitate USAIDs oversight of a large number of project grants and improve the ability of USAID and its grants office in U.S. Embassy Tel Aviv to take timely action as necessary. c. To provide the required technical and administrative support for the above and associated activities, including the capacity to provide technical feedback on possible overlap of new submissions with previous projects, assessing the applicant investigators' responses to technical provisos and the maintenance of program files and database

title.narrative: Institutional and Technical Support Services (ITSS II)
Services d'appui institutionnel et technique (ITSS II)
Services d'appui institutionnel et technique (ITSS II)

description.narrative: Under the Institutional and Technical Support Services contract (ITSS), ZemiTek coordinates with USAID AFR, the Office of Sustainable Development (AFR/SD) and its primary contributors: Power Africa, Trade Africa, and Young African Leadership Initiative (YALI). We support the implementation of activities and offer USAID AFR reliable, high-quality short- and long-term institutional, professional, technical, operational, and support services that include analytical, advisory, management, logistical, publications, conference and events planning and assist with special projects for multiple USAID technical sectors.

Dans le cadre du contrat de services d'appui institutionnel et technique (ITSS), ZemiTek se coordonne avec l'USAID AFR, le Bureau du développement durable (AFR/SD) et ses principaux contributeurs : Power Africa, Trade Africa et Young African Leadership Initiative (YALI). Nous soutenons la mise en œuvre des activités et offrons à l'USAID AFR des services institutionnels, professionnels, techniques, opérationnels et de soutien fiables et de haute qualité à court et à long terme qui comprennent l'analyse, le conseil, la gestion, la logistique, les publications, la planification de conférences et d'événements et une assistance à des projets spéciaux pour plusieurs secteurs techniques de l'USAID.

title.narrative: Project Last Mile
Projeto Última Milha

description.narrative: By leveraging the expertise and network of the Coca-Cola System, Project Last Mile is a pioneering public-private partnership with The Coca-Cola Company and Foundation, the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, The Global Fund, and USAID to help improve uptake of life-saving health services and to enable medicines to go tothe last mile and benefit communities in Africa. Project Last Mile collaborates with regional Coca-Colabottlers and suppliers to strengthen public health systems capacityin supply chain by sharing the expertise and network of the Coca-Cola System with the local Ministry of Health (MoH).

Ao aproveitar a experiência e a rede do Sistema Coca-Cola, o Project Last Mile é uma parceria público-privada pioneira com a The Coca-Cola Company and Foundation, a Fundação Bill e Melinda Gates, o Fundo Global e a USAID para ajudar a melhorar a utilização de serviços de saúde que salvam vidas e para permitir que os medicamentos cheguem à última milha e beneficiem as comunidades em África. O Projeto Last Mile colabora com engarrafadores e fornecedores regionais da Coca-Cola para fortalecer a capacidade dos sistemas de saúde pública na cadeia de abastecimento, compartilhando a experiência e a rede do Sistema Coca-Cola com o Ministério da Saúde (MS) local.

title.narrative: Critical Infrastructure Digitalization and Resilience (CIDR)

description.narrative: (Europe and Eurasia Regional): The Critical Infrastructure Digitalization and Resilience (CIDR) activity supports host governments and critical infrastructure sector entities in electric/natural gas/water transmission and distribution, electric power generation, telecom, district heating, oil, health care, transportation, and finance/banking improve their cybersecurity protection and response capabilities in the following areas:(1)the incorporation of cybersecurity best practices into organizational operations, planning, and procurement;(2)the prioritization of cyber security investment needs;(3)the selection of appropriate standards and corresponding security controls; and(4)establishment of legal and regulatory framework, as well as coordination bodies for region-wide cybersecurity information sharing. ..Through regional working groups/targeted technical assistance, CIDR focuses on (1)accelerating the development of the workforce among critical infrastructure entities and host governments to protect against and respond to threats from malign actors, particularly cyberattacks; (2) empowering governments and critical infrastructure entities in E&E to identify and address threats to critical infrastructure, and facilitate the export of U.S. technology and expertise to counter these threats;(3)establishing the policies, frameworks and coordination bodies necessary to empower critical infrastructure entities to protect and improve the resilience of critical infrastructure key resources;(4)developing robust information sharing networks between national and regional critical infrastructure entities, promoting coordinated and collaborative responses to threats to critical infrastructure; and (5) improving U.S. security through application of lessons learned from this USAID-supported activity by U.S. critical infrastructure entities. CIDR is funded through the E&E regional OU budget and Mission buy-ins. ..CIDR contributes to JRS Objective 3.2 and CAATSA Goal 1. . .

title.narrative: CW: Partnership for Living Better: Affordable, Accessible, Adaptable Sanitation Solutions (LIXIL)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Resilience and Food Security (RFS)): Purpose: The purpose of the Partnership for Better Living activity, a collaboration between USAID and LIXIL Group's Safe Toilet (SATO) business unit, is to increase sustained household access to sanitation and increase adoption of key hygiene behaviors through market-based approaches. This activity will explore and expand upon USAID experience with market-based sanitation including contextual business models, supply chains, and public policies for introduction and expansion of sanitation products and services. This Activity aims to demonstrate how to partner effectively with a large multinational company within the sanitation value chain in USAID Water for the World High Priority and Strategy-Aligned Countries. The partnership aims to reach at least 2 million people, which by the end of year 5, will have toilets in their homes installed with affordable LIXIL SATO products...Activities: Through the Partnership for Better Living activity, USAID will collaborate with LIXIL to expand the market for affordable and appropriate sanitation solutions and improve the availability of products and reliability of supply chains in countries of shared interest, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia. Global and country level activities under this partnership and cooperative agreement will focus on: 1.) expanding the market and increasing demand for household sanitation products and services; 2.) improving the availability of products and reliability of supply chains; and 3.) supporting partnerships with other global and local sanitation stakeholders and advancing global knowledge of market-based solutions to sanitation challenges. USAID and LIXIL will identify up to 12 partnership priority countries at the planning stage and in consultation with Missions to meet demands for their bilateral sanitation and hygiene investments. . .Benefitting Countries: (To be determined post-award)

title.narrative: DRG: PIDR Global Labor Program - Inclusive Futures (GLP-IF)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Development, Democracy, and Innovation (D): GLP-Inclusive Futures (GLP-IF) is implemented by a broad and diverse coalition of local and international institutions led by Sightsavers. GLP-IF tests an integrated systems approach for advancing the labor rights of people with disabilities, especially women, in Kenya. This approach could serve as a model for other contexts and other ultra-marginalized populations. Through GLP-IF, USAID will continue in Year-2 with FY 2022 funds to build relationships among workers, unions, non-governmental organizations, government, and companies to implement four interlocking workstreams:.1: Increasing access to decent work for persons with disabilities, particularly women workers - including in the climate-smart agriculture sector..2: Building the capacities of Kenyan trade unions and disabled persons' organizations (DPOs) to increasingly support women and men with disabilities by promoting and protecting labor rights..3: Influencing and building capacities among brands and value chain employers to develop, apply and measure rights-respecting employment and operational policies..4: Policy advocacy with the Government of Kenya to improve labor rights legislation and enforcement..GLP-IF directly contributes to the Multilateral Partnership for Organizing, Worker Empowerment, and Rights (M-POWER) initiative, which is a key deliverable of the Presidential Initiative for Democratic Renewal (PIDR) that USAID collaborates on with the Department of Labor and U.S. Department of State's Bureau for Democracy, Rights, and Labor (DRL)..

title.narrative: Discovery & Exploration of Emerging Pathogens - Viral Zoonoses (DEEP VZN)
Découverte et exploration de pathogènes émergents - Zoonoses virales (DEEP VZN)
Descubrimiento y exploración de patógenos emergentes: zoonosis virales (DEEP VZN)

description.narrative: DEEP VZN is a critical next step in the evolution of USAID's work to understand and address the risks posed by zoonotic diseases that can be transmitted from animals to humans. DEEP VZN will work in targeted countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America that have both a high risk for viral spillover and the capacity to safely conduct viral discovery. Identifying and understanding unknown viral threats will help these countriesand the worldbe better prepared to detect, prevent and respond to future biological threats.

DEEP VZN constitue une prochaine étape cruciale dans l'évolution du travail de l'USAID visant à comprendre et à traiter les risques posés par les maladies zoonotiques pouvant être transmises des animaux aux humains. DEEP VZN travaillera dans des pays ciblés d’Afrique, d’Asie et d’Amérique latine qui présentent à la fois un risque élevé de propagation virale et la capacité de mener des découvertes virales en toute sécurité. Identifier et comprendre les menaces virales inconnues aideront ces pays et le monde à être mieux préparés à détecter, prévenir et répondre aux futures menaces biologiques.

DEEP VZN es un siguiente paso fundamental en la evolución del trabajo de USAID para comprender y abordar los riesgos que plantean las enfermedades zoonóticas que pueden transmitirse de animales a humanos. DEEP VZN trabajará en países específicos de África, Asia y América Latina que tienen un alto riesgo de propagación viral y la capacidad de realizar descubrimientos virales de manera segura. Identificar y comprender amenazas virales desconocidas ayudará a estos países y al mundo a estar mejor preparados para detectar, prevenir y responder a futuras amenazas biológicas.

title.narrative: SCALING AN INNOVATIVE COMMUNITY-RUN ECCE PROGRAMME IN GHANA.

description.narrative: worldwide, more than 250 million young childrenthe majority of whom are in low- and middle-income countriesare at risk of not achieving their developmental potential due to poverty, poor health and nutrition, and deficient care and stimulation. to improve early childhood care and education (ecce) and school readiness, education partners are supporting the government of ghana to run parent-led, low-cost, highly effective educational playgroups for children ages four to six. a randomized controlled trial (rct) on education partners model found that the ecce program significantly improves child development, including cognitive, socio-emotional, and health, which are critical components of school readiness. as the government starts to implement the model, education partners are training education officials and teachers to prepare and empower mothers to run playgroups at their childrens kindergartens. with support from development innovation ventures, education partners will work with the government of ghana to scale the program from six to 36 districts and catalyze funding to reach 60 districtsincluding 1.2 million childrenacross the northern region by the end of 2028.

title.narrative: Building Scalable Model for Personalized Learning in Indian Public Schools

description.narrative: To enable individualized instruction in classrooms with limited resources, education technology company Educational Initiatives (Ei) developed Mindspark, a personal adaptive learning (PAL) software that identifies individual student learning levels in math, the predominant local language, and English through diagnostic tests. It then provides targeted instruction to help students learn at a level and pace most appropriate for them. Mindspark is one of only a few rigorously-tested PAL software programs in India and has demonstrated significant and cost-effective learning gains in independent evaluations, including a randomized controlled trial. Mindspark has been used by 500,000 students and is available in nine languages on tablets, laptops, and computers. With support from Development Innovation Ventures (DIV), Ei will make Mindspark accessible to students in public schools, reaching 40,000 students and 1,000 teachers across 200 government day schools over three years.

title.narrative: Private Sector Productivity

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

title.narrative: Balkan Media Assistance Program

description.narrative: USAID seeks to strengthen the competitiveness of independent media in the Western Balkans in the local and regional marketplaces, and improve the sustainability of the sector across the region through creative partnerships and collaboration. Operating in five countries, including Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia, this effort will build upon the current Balkan Media Assistance Program (BMAP) activity to address these areas and provide a more data-driven, collective, and impactful approach. While BMAP has helped beneficiaries become more revenue-ready, BMAP forward will help beneficiaries continue to advance in this area for some, while for others, it will ensure that they become investment-ready. The objectives of this activity are as follows: Objective 1: Increase strategic business practices of key media partners to operate as viable enterprises and better understand their markets and audiences. Objective 2: Reinforce the ability of content producers to produce data-driven content, engage wider audiences, improve digital security efforts, and expand reach across the region. Objective 3: Foster stronger partnerships between media outlets and the technology, commercial, and entrepreneurial sectors to advance solutions on common challenges in the information space.

title.narrative: PO: Global Empowerment of Underrepresented Students and Minorities in Agriculture Natural Resources, and Related Sciences (MANNRS)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Resilience and Food Security (RFS)): Purpose: USAID seeks to strengthen its commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility (DEIA) in the workforce and across its partnerships and programming through deliberate and intentional efforts. The purpose of this activity is to improve global food- and water-security through the empowerment of individuals from backgrounds underrepresented in the agriculture, natural resources and related science fields..Activities: .This activity supports the professional development of underrepresented minorities and increases awareness of career and partnership opportunities within the climate, agriculture, food security and water sectors..Activities include:.In-person and virtual engagements facilitated between development practitioners, academic and professional organizations, and students from underrepresented minority backgrounds, including intersectional identities such as LGBTQI+ and persons with disabilities, that include technical presentations and professional development trainings.Trainings and resource materials, including on gender and social inclusion in food and water security programming, disseminated in various fora targeted at underrepresented minorities.Global and food security programming, events and opportunities promoted through digital and print materials targeted at minorities underrepresented in agriculture, natural resources, and related sciences, including integration of gender into that programming .A Global Empowerment Fellows Leadership Program implemented to prepare undergraduate and graduate students for international development fieldwork and global citizenship through training and experiential learning..Benefitting Countries: Global.

title.narrative: CA: New FTFIL for Horticulture
CA : Nouveau FTFIL pour l'horticulture

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Resilience and Food Security (RFS)): Purpose: The purpose is to identify and strengthen opportunities for smallholder farmers to develop and sustainably manage horticulture-based enterprises in Feed the Future production systems, including research and local capacity development on 1) climate-resilient management of nutrient-dense food and 2) inclusive horticultural business growth and commercialization, with a focus on youth opportunity, gender equality and women's empowerment. .$2 million of funding within this IM contributes to meeting the required "Research and Development" directive of $148.8 million and the required "Feed the Future Innovation Labs" sub-directive of $58 million..Activities: A portfolio of research programs across the biophysical and social sciences supporting horticulture food production has been developed that are central to advancing novel solutions that support global efforts to reduce hunger, poverty, and malnutrition. The activities are being designed through a broad consultative process with the stakeholder community to identify the best options for research interventions in horticulture, increase the capacity of local agriculture innovation systems, and provide opportunities to individuals and organizations in partner countries to improve their own capacities, skills, and knowledge. .Benefiting Countries: Honduras, Ghana, Kenya, Nepal, Guatemala, Haiti, Nigeria, Rwanda, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda...

(Bureau de l'USAID pour la résilience et la sécurité alimentaire (RFS)) : Objectif : L'objectif est d'identifier et de renforcer les opportunités permettant aux petits exploitants agricoles de développer et de gérer de manière durable des entreprises horticoles dans les systèmes de production Feed the Future, y compris la recherche et le développement des capacités locales sur 1) la gestion résiliente au climat des aliments riches en nutriments et 2) la croissance et la commercialisation inclusives des entreprises horticoles, en mettant l'accent sur les opportunités pour les jeunes, l'égalité des sexes et l'autonomisation des femmes. Un financement de 2 millions de dollars au sein de cette GI contribue à répondre à la directive « Recherche et développement » requise de 148,8 millions de dollars et à la sous-directive requise « Nourrir les futurs laboratoires d'innovation » de 58 millions de dollars. Les activités sont conçues dans le cadre d'un vaste processus consultatif avec la communauté des parties prenantes pour identifier les meilleures options d'interventions de recherche en horticulture, accroître la capacité des systèmes d'innovation agricole locaux et offrir des opportunités aux individus et aux organisations des pays partenaires d'améliorer leurs propres capacités, compétences et connaissances. .Pays bénéficiaires : Honduras, Ghana, Kenya, Népal, Guatemala, Haïti, Nigeria, Rwanda, Tanzanie, Thaïlande, Ouganda...

title.narrative: Current and Emerging Threats to Crops Innovation Lab
Menaces actuelles et émergentes pour le laboratoire d'innovation en matière de cultures.
Menaces actuelles et émergentes pour le laboratoire d'innovation en matière de cultures.
Menaces actuelles et émergentes pour le laboratoire d'innovation en matière de cultures.

description.narrative: The activity will design, lead, and implement an applied research program focused on the control of current and emerging biotic threats to food security crops that the poor depend on. The program will also strengthen local research partners through capacity development while benefiting smallholder farmers and other beneficiaries of USAID assistance. The Innovation Lab will serve as a resource to USAID Missions and their implementing partners in their efforts to overcome critical crop pest, weed and disease constraints facing their national food systems. The Innovation Lab is broadly expected to help recognize, build on and influence impact pathways from crop biotic threat protection research to development outcomes through partnerships with USAID Mission-supported programs, national partners, private companies, community-based organizations, and other donors and their programs.

L'activité concevra, dirigera et mettra en œuvre un programme de recherche appliquée axé sur le contrôle des menaces biotiques actuelles et émergentes pour les cultures de sécurité alimentaire dont dépendent les pauvres. Le programme renforcera également les partenaires de recherche locaux grâce au développement des capacités tout en bénéficiant aux petits exploitants agricoles et aux autres bénéficiaires de l'aide de l'USAID. Le laboratoire d'innovation servira de ressource aux missions de l'USAID et à leurs partenaires de mise en œuvre dans leurs efforts pour surmonter les contraintes critiques liées aux ravageurs, aux mauvaises herbes et aux maladies auxquelles sont confrontés leurs systèmes alimentaires nationaux. Le laboratoire d'innovation devrait largement contribuer à reconnaître, à développer et à influencer les voies d'impact depuis la recherche sur la protection des cultures contre les menaces biotiques jusqu'aux résultats de développement grâce à des partenariats avec les programmes soutenus par la mission de l'USAID, des partenaires nationaux, des entreprises privées, des organisations communautaires et d'autres donateurs et leurs programmes.

title.narrative: PA: Surveys for Monitoring in Resilience and Food Security (SMRFS)
PA : Enquêtes de suivi de la résilience et de la sécurité alimentaire (SMRFS)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Resilience and Food Security (RFS)): . .Purpose: The purpose of the Surveys for Monitoring in RFS (SMRFS) is to support the collection and use of high-quality population-based survey data in USAID's Bureau for Resilience priority countries; to strengthen population-based data collection, analysis and use capacities of local organizations; and support the development of a range of innovative approaches to streamline data collection and improve data quality. . .Activities: SMRFS' primary activity is to carry out all the necessary tasks to plan, implement and report on population-based household surveys (PBS) to collect data on resilience, food security, agriculture, nutrition, and water, sanitation and hygiene in RFS priority countries. SMRFS will also strengthen local capacity to plan, collect, analyze and use PBS data; disseminate communications materials on PBS results for a range of audiences; maintain a state-of-the-art, step-by-step toolkit on how to implement high-quality surveys and collect and analyze key indicators on poverty, food insecurity, resilience, nutrition and WASH and make it available as a public good; provide technical assistance to users of the toolkit; provide on-demand analysis of PBS data to design streamlined data collection instruments; better understand gender and age dynamics within the targeted areas and validate theories of change; and develop guidance on alternative data collection methods when face-to-face data collection is not possible. ...Benefitting Countries: Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Mali, Nepal, Nigeria, Uganda.

(Bureau de l'USAID pour la résilience et la sécurité alimentaire (RFS)) : . .Objectif : L'objectif des enquêtes de suivi dans le RFS (SMRFS) est de soutenir la collecte et l'utilisation de données d'enquête de haute qualité basées sur la population dans les pays prioritaires du Bureau pour la résilience de l'USAID ; renforcer les capacités de collecte, d’analyse et d’utilisation de données démographiques des organisations locales ; et soutenir le développement d’une gamme d’approches innovantes pour rationaliser la collecte de données et améliorer la qualité des données. . .Activités : L'activité principale du SMRFS est d'effectuer toutes les tâches nécessaires pour planifier, mettre en œuvre et rendre compte des enquêtes auprès des ménages basées sur la population (PBS) afin de collecter des données sur la résilience, la sécurité alimentaire, l'agriculture, la nutrition, l'eau, l'assainissement et l'hygiène dans les pays prioritaires de la RFS. Le SMRFS renforcera également la capacité locale à planifier, collecter, analyser et utiliser les données PBS ; diffuser des supports de communication sur les résultats du PBS auprès d'un large public ; maintenir une boîte à outils de pointe, étape par étape, sur la manière de mettre en œuvre des enquêtes de haute qualité, de collecter et d'analyser des indicateurs clés sur la pauvreté, l'insécurité alimentaire, la résilience, la nutrition et WASH et de la rendre disponible en tant que bien public ; fournir une assistance technique aux utilisateurs de la boîte à outils ; fournir une analyse à la demande des données PBS pour concevoir des instruments rationalisés de collecte de données ; mieux comprendre les dynamiques de genre et d’âge dans les domaines ciblés et valider les théories du changement ; et élaborer des orientations sur les méthodes alternatives de collecte de données lorsque la collecte de données en face à face n'est pas possible. ...Pays bénéficiaires : Éthiopie, Ghana, Kenya, Mali, Népal, Nigeria, Ouganda.

title.narrative: Urban Resilient Water Security, Sanitation, and Hygiene Program

description.narrative: The program aims to promote sustainable and climate-resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and water resources management (WRM) policy in urban and peri-urban areas, and to strengthen the evidence base for decision making for host governments at local, regional and national levels. The activity will generate new evidence and allow USAID to address critical knowledge and learning gaps related to achieving the goal of increasing the availability and management of safe water and sanitation for the worlds most vulnerable.

description.narrative: The purpose of the activity is to acquire non-direct education support services for DDI Center for Education and USAID Missions to supplement its direct-hire staff, i.e., federal civilian employees that are appointed under civil service and foreign service.

(Bureau de l'USAID pour le développement, la démocratie et l'innovation (D) : Cette activité permettra au Centre pour l'éducation de l'USAID, ainsi qu'à d'autres unités opérationnelles de l'USAID, de recruter et d'embaucher du personnel technique, professionnel, opérationnel et de soutien sous contrat, à long terme et à court terme, pour répondre à une gamme de besoins, y compris l'accès à de nouveaux domaines d'expertise pour aider l'USAID à répondre à l'impact du COVID-19 sur les systèmes éducatifs. Les fonds de l'exercice 22 soutiendront environ 25 consultants techniques à long terme dans DDI/EDU, en plus de nombreux consultants à court terme, fournira une assistance technique ainsi qu'un soutien opérationnel pour la mise en œuvre de la stratégie du gouvernement américain sur l'éducation de base internationale et de la politique éducative de l'USAID, qui nécessitent toutes deux du personnel possédant de nouveaux domaines d'expertise technique pour fournir un soutien opportun dans le monde entier.

(Oficina de Desarrollo, Democracia e Innovación (D) de USAID: esta actividad permitirá que el Centro para la Educación de USAID, así como otras unidades operativas de USAID, recluten y contraten personal técnico, profesional, operativo y de apoyo contratado, tanto a largo como a corto plazo, para responder a una variedad de necesidades, incluido el acceso a nuevas áreas de experiencia para ayudar a USAID a responder al impacto de COVID-19 en los sistemas educativos. Los fondos del año fiscal 22 apoyarán aproximadamente a 25 consultores técnicos a largo plazo en DDI/EDU Además de numerosas consultorías a corto plazo, los consultores brindarán asistencia técnica y apoyo operativo para la implementación de la Estrategia del Gobierno de los EE. UU. sobre Educación Básica Internacional y la Política Educativa de USAID, las cuales requieren personal con nuevas áreas de experiencia técnica para brindar apoyo oportuno en todo el mundo.

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): The primary focus of the RISSA mechanism is crucial research and institutional support to AFR, ensuring that it is able to achieve the following goals of the Africa Joint Regional Strategy: 1) Advance Mutual Peace and Security Interests; 2) Increase Mutually Beneficial Economic Growth, Trade, and Investment; 3) Strengthen Democracy, Human Rights, and Good Governance; and 4) Promote Inclusive Country-led Development. AFR would use the long-term and short-term technical expertise and services obtained through this contract to build the capacity and deepen the commitment of development partners in Africa and provide critical staff support. This mechanism will support the extension of various consultancies within GH/ID.

(USAID Global Health (GH)) : L'objectif principal du mécanisme RISSA est la recherche cruciale et le soutien institutionnel à l'AFR, garantissant qu'il est en mesure d'atteindre les objectifs suivants de la Stratégie régionale commune pour l'Afrique : 1) Promouvoir les intérêts mutuels en matière de paix et de sécurité ; 2) Accroître la croissance économique, le commerce et les investissements mutuellement bénéfiques ; 3) Renforcer la démocratie, les droits de l'homme et la bonne gouvernance ; et 4) Promouvoir un développement inclusif dirigé par les pays. AFR utiliserait l’expertise technique et les services à long terme et à court terme obtenus dans le cadre de ce contrat pour renforcer les capacités et approfondir l’engagement des partenaires de développement en Afrique et fournir un soutien essentiel en termes de personnel. Ce mécanisme soutiendra l'extension de diverses consultations au sein de GH/ID.

A AFR utilizaria os conhecimentos técnicos e os serviços de longo e curto prazo obtidos através deste contrato para desenvolver a capacidade e aprofundar o compromisso dos parceiros de desenvolvimento em África e fornecer apoio crítico ao pessoal. Este mecanismo apoiará a extensão de diversas consultorias dentro do GH/ID.

title.narrative: DRG: OASIS Institutional Support Contract
DRG: Contrato de Apoyo Institucional a OASIS

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Development, Democracy, and Innovation (D): DDI/DRG will support a task order to procure support staff under the General Services Administration's One Acquisition Solution for Integrated Services (OASIS) and OASIS Small Business (SB) contracts, which provide Best in Class (BIC) flexible and innovative solutions for complex professional services. USAID is strongly encouraged by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to use BIC mechanisms. Staff funded under OASIS will include program support, management, and administrative staff. The contract will also include the ability to hire short and medium-term specialists for unanticipated needs. Positions include but are not limited to administrative assistants, program assistants, a communications specialist, a human resources specialist, a travel specialist, and technical consultants in democracy, human rights, and governance to meet on-demand Mission and DRG Center needs. The OASIS task order also includes a fund manager for the Center. This person will monitor several funds activities encompassing the Elections and Political Processes and Human Rights Grants Program funds. Program and OE funding supports the costs of these staff...With FY 2022 resources, DDI/DRG will also fund a senior consultant to revise and update the existing Integrating Gender into DRG Programming Toolkit (2016) and short-term technical assistance through one or more consultants to develop new tools and resources for Center staff and the DRG cadre to facilitate gender inclusive programming through OASIS..

(Oficina de USAID para el Desarrollo, la Democracia y la Innovación (D): DDI/DRG apoyará una orden de trabajo para adquirir personal de apoyo bajo los contratos One Acquisition Solution for Integrated Services (OASIS) y OASIS Small Business (SB) de la Administración de Servicios Generales, que brindan soluciones flexibles e innovadoras de la mejor clase (BIC) para servicios profesionales complejos. La Oficina de Gestión y Presupuesto (OMB) recomienda encarecidamente a USAID que utilice mecanismos BIC. El personal financiado bajo OASIS incluirá apoyo, gestión y El contrato también incluirá la capacidad de contratar especialistas a corto y mediano plazo para necesidades imprevistas. Los puestos incluyen, entre otros, asistentes administrativos, asistentes de programas, un especialista en comunicaciones, un especialista en recursos humanos, un especialista en viajes y consultores técnicos en democracia, derechos humanos y gobernanza para satisfacer las necesidades bajo demanda del Centro DRG. Esta persona monitoreará varias actividades de fondos que abarcan los fondos del Programa de Subvenciones para Elecciones y Procesos Políticos y Derechos Humanos. El financiamiento del programa y la OE respalda los costos de este personal... Con recursos del año fiscal 2022, DDI/DRG también financiará un consultor senior para revisar y actualizar el conjunto de herramientas de programación de integración de género en los DRG (2016) existente y asistencia técnica a corto plazo a través de uno o más consultores para desarrollar nuevas herramientas y recursos para el personal del Centro y el cuadro del DRG para facilitar la programación inclusiva de género a través de OASIS..

title.narrative: Green Recovery Investment Platform (GRIP)
Plateforme d'investissement pour la relance verte (GRIP)
Plataforma de Inversión para la Recuperación Verde (GRIP)
Plataforma de Inversión para la Recuperación Verde (GRIP)

description.narrative: (USAID Africa Regional): The Green Recovery Investment Platform (GRIP) is a global flagship climate finance activity that will mobilize private finance and private sector actions that support the transition to an equitable and resilient net-zero economy while stimulating recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic. These investments will support diverse climate change mitigation and adaptation activities aligned with implementing country-driven Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) under the Paris Climate Accord. Using FY 2022 funds, USAID AFR Regional will strengthen Missions' capacity to mobilize private and public finance towards climate mitigation projects that support natural climate solutions and help countries to meet their NDCs. Key focus areas will be addressing policy barriers and creating incentives, convening public and private sector actors to increase capital flows, and building the deal flow pipeline...Examples could include: organizing an "Innovative Finance for Nature" workshop in Africa to identify, explore, and cultivate partnerships for financing conservation, developing a customized toolkit for achieving community benefits in carbon markets projects in 1-2 countries, or providing local banks and financial institutions in sub-Saharan Africa with in-person training and tools focused on climate financing, climate risk, and carbon footprinting, to increase climate lending capacity...$1,200,000 of FY 2022 funds for this IM contribute to USAID AFR Regional's Sustainable Landscapes directive of $3,000,000. $300,000 of FY 2022 funds for this IM contribute to USAID AFR Regional's Adaptation directive of $3,100,000...

(USAID Afrique Régionale) : La Plateforme d’investissement pour la relance verte (GRIP) est une activité phare mondiale de financement climatique qui mobilisera des financements privés et des actions du secteur privé qui soutiennent la transition vers une économie nette zéro équitable et résiliente tout en stimulant la reprise après la pandémie de COVID-19. Ces investissements soutiendront diverses activités d’atténuation et d’adaptation au changement climatique alignées sur la mise en œuvre des contributions déterminées au niveau national (CDN) et des plans nationaux d’adaptation (PAN) dans le cadre de l’Accord de Paris sur le climat. Grâce aux fonds de l'exercice 2022, l'USAID AFR Regional renforcera la capacité des missions à mobiliser des financements privés et publics vers des projets d'atténuation du climat qui soutiennent des solutions climatiques naturelles et aideront les pays à atteindre leurs CDN. Les principaux domaines d'intervention consisteront à éliminer les obstacles politiques et à créer des incitations, à réunir les acteurs des secteurs public et privé pour augmenter les flux de capitaux et à construire le pipeline de flux de transactions... Des exemples pourraient inclure : l'organisation d'un atelier « Finance innovante pour la nature » en Afrique pour identifier, explorer et cultiver des partenariats pour le financement de la conservation, le développement d'une boîte à outils personnalisée pour obtenir des avantages communautaires dans les projets de marchés du carbone dans 1 à 2 pays, ou la fourniture aux banques et institutions financières locales en Afrique subsaharienne d'une formation en personne et d'outils axés sur le financement climatique, le risque climatique et l'empreinte carbone, pour augmenter la capacité de prêt climatique... 1 200 000 $ des fonds de l'exercice 2022 pour cette GI contribuent à la directive régionale sur les paysages durables de l'USAID AFR de 3 000 000 $. 300 000 $ de fonds pour l'exercice 2022 pour cette GI contribuent à la directive d'adaptation de l'USAID AFR Regional de 3 100 000 $...

(USAID África Regional): La Plataforma de Inversión para la Recuperación Verde (GRIP) es una actividad emblemática mundial de financiación climática que movilizará el financiamiento privado y las acciones del sector privado que apoyan la transición a una economía neta cero equitativa y resiliente al tiempo que estimulan la recuperación de la pandemia de COVID-19. Estas inversiones apoyarán diversas actividades de mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático alineadas con la implementación de Contribuciones Determinadas a Nivel Nacional (NDC) y Planes Nacionales de Adaptación (PAN) impulsados ​​por los países en el marco del Acuerdo Climático de París. Utilizando fondos del año fiscal 2022, USAID AFR Regional fortalecerá la capacidad de las Misiones para movilizar financiamiento público y privado hacia proyectos de mitigación climática que respalden soluciones climáticas naturales y ayuden a los países a cumplir con sus NDC. Las áreas clave de enfoque serán abordar las barreras políticas y crear incentivos, convocar a actores de los sectores público y privado para aumentar los flujos de capital y construir el flujo de acuerdos... Los ejemplos podrían incluir: organizar un taller de "Finanzas innovadoras para la naturaleza" en África para identificar, explorar y cultivar asociaciones para financiar la conservación, desarrollar un conjunto de herramientas personalizado para lograr beneficios comunitarios en proyectos de mercados de carbono en 1 o 2 países, o proporcionar a los bancos e instituciones financieras locales en el África subsahariana capacitación y herramientas en persona centradas en el financiamiento climático, riesgo y huella de carbono para aumentar la capacidad de préstamo climático... $1,200,000 de los fondos del año fiscal 2022 para este IM contribuyen a la directiva de Paisajes Sostenibles de USAID AFR Regional de $3,000,000. $300,000 de los fondos del año fiscal 2022 para este IM contribuyen a la directiva de adaptación de USAID AFR Regional de $3,100,000...

description.narrative: Feed the Future striga smart sorghum for africa walking through a field of sorghum, your vision might be drawn upwards to the plants impressively tall stalks, its waxy green leaves or its large panicles. you may be unaware of what is happening to the crops under your feet. a cereal species of the grass family (poaceae), sorghum is an important crop worldwide. Its edible starchy seeds are used for food it is a staple in sub-saharan africa, where it is primarily ground into flour and made into a stiff porridge. it can also be used for the production of alcoholic beverages and biofuels, and the stalks and leaves can be used as animal fodder or building materials. despite its good adaptation to african growing conditions, the crop suffers from multiple production constraints. underfoot, you will find the two most urgent constraints: poor soils, and infestation by a parasitic weed called striga also known as witchweed as it causes damage to the host plant when it is still in its invisible underground stages. striga parasitises sorghum through its roots, resulting in severe yield reductions. the project aims to overcome the above constraints. as striga cannot be controlled sustainably by a stand-alone technique, the project aims to improve and combine two approaches: deploying sorghum cultivars with increased levels of striga resistance, and applying fertilisers.

title.narrative: REALIZING EQUITABLE ACCESS, RETENTION, AND COMPLETION IN HIGHER EDUCATION (REACH)
LOGRAR UN ACCESO, RETENCIÓN Y FINALIZACIÓN EQUITATIVOS EN LA EDUCACIÓN SUPERIOR (REACH)

description.narrative: Realizing equitable access, retention, and completion in higher education (REACH) will play a critical role in improving access to market-relevant higher education (he) and training in the three target countries of guatemala, honduras and paraguay by strengthening hei capacity to provide scholarships and wrap-around services to marginalized populations who are attending or planning to pursue postsecondary education, and increase youth employability in prioritized, growing, and formal economic sectors.

Lograr el acceso, la retención y la finalización equitativos de la educación superior (REACH) desempeñará un papel fundamental en la mejora del acceso a la educación superior (he) relevante para el mercado y a la capacitación en los tres países objetivo: guatemala, honduras y paraguay, al fortalecer la capacidad de las ies para proporcionar becas y servicios integrales a las poblaciones marginadas que asisten o planean seguir una educación postsecundaria, y aumentar la empleabilidad de los jóvenes en sectores económicos priorizados, en crecimiento y formales.

description.narrative: the purpose of propel health (round 1) is to improve the enabling environment for equitable and sustainable health services, supplies, and delivery systems through policy development and implementation; adequate, predictable and sustainable financing; enhanced government stewardship, transparency, and accountability; and use of evidence-based advocacy approaches at the global, national and sub-national levels to promote best practices.

L'objectif de Propuls Health (cycle 1) est d'améliorer l'environnement propice à des services, des fournitures et des systèmes de prestation de santé équitables et durables grâce à l'élaboration et à la mise en œuvre de politiques ; un financement adéquat, prévisible et durable ; une gestion gouvernementale, une transparence et une responsabilisation améliorées ; et l'utilisation d'approches de plaidoyer fondées sur des données probantes aux niveaux mondial, national et infranational pour promouvoir les meilleures pratiques.

el propósito de impulsar la salud (ronda 1) es mejorar el entorno propicio para servicios, suministros y sistemas de prestación de salud equitativos y sostenibles mediante el desarrollo y la implementación de políticas; financiación adecuada, predecible y sostenible; mayor administración, transparencia y rendición de cuentas del gobierno; y el uso de enfoques de promoción basados ​​en evidencia a nivel global, nacional y subnacional para promover las mejores prácticas.

title.narrative: DRG: Rapid Response for Justice, Rights and Security
GRD: Respuesta Rápida por la Justicia, los Derechos y la Seguridad

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Development, Democracy, and Innovation (D): DDI/DRG intends to use FY 2022 funds for its new Justice, Rights, and Security Rapid Response activity (JRS-RRA). JRS-RRA is capable of providing fast, short-term support on justice, rights and security issues. This mechanism will build on the strengths and lessons learned of the existing rights-related rapid response mechanism (the Human Rights Support Mechanism), set to end in September 2023. It also advances the National Security Strategy by defending and protecting human rights and addressing discrimination, inequity, and marginalization in all its forms. .Over the past six years, DDI/DRG has developed a highly effective tool to help Missions respond to urgent and unforeseen needs. By using pre-positioned funds in a global mechanism, USAID is able to leverage our Missions' in-country expertise to identify and support local stakeholder-led responses to critical justice, rights, and security opportunities and challenges. These tools have allowed USAID to be a true first responder in recent contexts (e.g. Sudan, Nicaragua and Belarus), enabling local partners to respond to rapid shifts in contexts and needs. This past year, DRG commissioned a third-party evaluation of our rapid response work, which identified it as a critical and highly effective tool that allowed Missions and partners to respond to needs that would have otherwise gone unmet. .Based on the evaluation's findings, and with HRSM ending, DDI/DRG awarded JRS-RRA to provide timely, effective, and discreet support to local organizations around the world with justice, rights and security needs. This award will be managed by DDI/DRG but oriented towards supporting Mission-identified needs. A portion of funding will be used to protect human rights defenders and journalists expanding USAID's global response capabilities to urgent human rights needs and ensure continued responsiveness to Mission requests. $3,940,000 of ESF will count toward the $7M

(Oficina de USAID para el Desarrollo, la Democracia y la Innovación (D): DDI/DRG tiene la intención de utilizar fondos del año fiscal 2022 para su nueva actividad de Respuesta Rápida de Justicia, Derechos y Seguridad (JRS-RRA). El JRS-RRA es capaz de proporcionar apoyo rápido y a corto plazo en cuestiones de justicia, derechos y seguridad. Este mecanismo se basará en las fortalezas y lecciones aprendidas del mecanismo de respuesta rápida relacionado con los derechos existente (el Mecanismo de Apoyo a los Derechos Humanos), que finalizará en septiembre de 2023. También promueve la Estrategia de Seguridad Nacional defendiendo y protegiendo los derechos humanos y abordando la discriminación, la inequidad y la marginación en todas sus formas. Durante los últimos seis años, DDI/DRG ha desarrollado una herramienta altamente efectiva para ayudar a las Misiones a responder a necesidades urgentes e imprevistas. Al utilizar fondos preposicionados en un mecanismo global, USAID puede aprovechar la experiencia de nuestras Misiones en el país para identificar y apoyar respuestas lideradas por partes interesadas locales a oportunidades y desafíos críticos de justicia, derechos y seguridad. USAID debe ser un verdadero primer interviniente en contextos recientes (p. ej. Sudán, Nicaragua y Bielorrusia), permitiendo a los socios locales responder a cambios rápidos en contextos y necesidades. El año pasado, DRG encargó una evaluación independiente de nuestro trabajo de respuesta rápida, que lo identificó como una herramienta crítica y altamente efectiva que permitió a las Misiones y socios responder a necesidades que de otro modo no habrían quedado satisfechas. .Basado en los hallazgos de la evaluación, y con el HRSM finalizado, DDI/DRG premió al JRS-RRA por brindar apoyo oportuno, efectivo y discreto a organizaciones locales de todo el mundo con necesidades de justicia, derechos y seguridad. Esta subvención será administrada por DDI/DRG pero orientada a apoyar las necesidades identificadas por la Misión. Una parte de los fondos se utilizará para proteger a los defensores de los derechos humanos y a los periodistas, ampliando las capacidades de respuesta global de USAID a las necesidades urgentes de derechos humanos y garantizando una capacidad de respuesta continua a las solicitudes de la Misión. 3.940.000 dólares del FSE contarán para los 7 millones de dólares.

title.narrative: Propel Adapt
Propulser Adapt

description.narrative: Propel Adapt seeks to address policy, advocacy, financing, and governance challenges in fragile settings that cause barriers to care.

(USAID Global Health (GH)) : PROPEL Adapt renforce l'environnement favorable et renforce la résilience des systèmes de santé, y compris le système de soins de santé primaires, ainsi que la résilience des partenaires locaux dans le contexte de chocs, de facteurs de stress et dans des contextes fragiles. Le projet utilise des approches politiques, de plaidoyer, de financement de la santé et de gouvernance pour renforcer les capacités de résilience d'absorption, d'adaptation et de transformation des systèmes de santé afin de soutenir la capacité des pays à se préparer et à répondre en temps opportun à divers chocs et facteurs de stress, notamment les pandémies comme le COVID-19, les épidémies, les impacts du changement climatique, les conflits, les fluctuations du marché et autres. PROPEL Adapt travaille également à soutenir les missions travaillant dans le cadre du lien humanitaire-développement-paix pour soutenir la transition des contextes fragiles de la réponse humanitaire au développement avec un renforcement plus complet des systèmes de santé. Ce projet effectuera une évaluation dynamique des coûts d'ensembles d'avantages complets pour aider les pays à faire la transition vers la réintégration et/ou la fourniture de services complets de planification familiale et de santé reproductive (PF/SR) à la population touchée après une situation d'urgence ; il développera un outil de renforcement des capacités de plaidoyer en matière de PF/SR incluant le handicap pour permettre aux organisations locales de plaider en faveur de changements politiques qui améliorent et étendent l'accès et la qualité des services de PF/SR dans des situations de crise ; il se concentrera sur le renforcement de la gouvernance pour la préparation en matière de PF/SR grâce à l'évaluation des lacunes et des opportunités en matière de coordination ; et une activité de responsabilité sociale pour aider les communautés à garantir la disponibilité continue d'un accès équitable à la PF/SR lorsque des chocs surviennent.

title.narrative: SWIFT Staffing

description.narrative: The objective of this IDIQ is to provide USAIDs Office of Transition Initiatives (OTI) with the means to support U.S. foreign policy objectives by catalyzing local initiatives to advance stability, peace and democracy in response to complex political crises. USAID/OTIs program team, comprised of USAID/OTI and Contractor personnel, will work on the ground to seize emerging windows of opportunity to provide adaptive and agile programming.

title.narrative: Conflict Early Warning, Mitigation and Peace Building
Alerta temprana de conflictos, mitigación y consolidación de la paz
Alerta temprana de conflictos, mitigación y consolidación de la paz
Alerta temprana de conflictos, mitigación y consolidación de la paz

description.narrative: Reduce the threat or impact of violent conflict and promote peaceful resolution of differences, ensure conflict sensitivity so as not to exacerbate sources of violence and/or establish an inclusive framework for peace and reconciliation which addresses all key drivers and mitigators of conflict. This includes activities aimed specifically at atrocities prevention, as well as activities intended to transform relationships to decrease the likelihood of future violent conflict. Develop and support early warning and response mechanisms such as early warning models and response protocols; conflict analysis; monitoring mechanisms and peace structures at different levels; peace building communication systems; confidence-building measures; crisis-response planning and management skills at the local and national levels; and means for rapid and effective response in the event of crisis. Support quick-impact, outcome-based activities required to demonstrate the positive impact of a peace process, operation or other event, such as mobilizing small grants for communities and local/national governments; ensuring delivery of services (e.g., "ministry in a box"); bringing local and national government authorities closer to their constituencies (e.g., town hall meetings, consultations, production and dissemination of information); generating employment for potential spoilers; and managing expectations.

Reducir la amenaza o el impacto de un conflicto violento y promover la resolución pacífica de las diferencias, garantizar la sensibilidad al conflicto para no exacerbar las fuentes de violencia y/o establecer un marco inclusivo para la paz y la reconciliación que aborde todos los factores clave y mitigantes del conflicto. Esto incluye actividades dirigidas específicamente a la prevención de atrocidades, así como actividades destinadas a transformar las relaciones para disminuir la probabilidad de futuros conflictos violentos. Desarrollar y apoyar mecanismos de alerta temprana y respuesta, como modelos de alerta temprana y protocolos de respuesta; análisis de conflictos; mecanismos de seguimiento y estructuras de paz a diferentes niveles; sistemas de comunicación para la construcción de la paz; medidas de fomento de la confianza; habilidades de planificación y gestión de respuesta a crisis a nivel local y nacional; y medios para una respuesta rápida y eficaz en caso de crisis. Apoyar actividades de impacto rápido basadas en resultados necesarias para demostrar el impacto positivo de un proceso de paz, operación u otro evento, como movilizar pequeñas subvenciones para comunidades y gobiernos locales/nacionales; asegurar la prestación de servicios (por ejemplo, "ministerio en una caja"); acercar las autoridades gubernamentales locales y nacionales a sus electores (por ejemplo, reuniones públicas, consultas, producción y difusión de información); generar empleo para posibles saboteadores; y gestionar las expectativas.

description.narrative: The Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) activity provides monitoring, evaluation, learning, and knowledge management support services to USAID operating units (OUs) in the Central America region, including USAID/El Salvador; the USAID/Central America and Mexico (CAM) regional Mission; regional bilateral Missions in Guatemala, Nicaragua, Honduras, and Mexico; and USAID/Washington-based bureaus and offices operating in Central America.

La actividad de Monitoreo, Evaluación y Aprendizaje (MEL) brinda servicios de apoyo de monitoreo, evaluación, aprendizaje y gestión del conocimiento a las unidades operativas (OU) de USAID en la región de Centroamérica, incluida USAID/El Salvador; la Misión regional USAID/Centroamérica y México (CAM); Misiones bilaterales regionales en Guatemala, Nicaragua, Honduras y México; y oficinas y oficinas con sede en Washington/USAID que operan en Centroamérica.

title.narrative: Evaluating Impact of FCAP on Poverty Alleviation & Citizen Engagement in Rwanda

description.narrative: community-driven development (cdd) programswhere community members define, implement, and maintain externally-funded public infrastructure projectshave not significantly reduced poverty, despite their wide use. studies find that cdd programs often fail to deliver due to poor facilitation, low civic engagement, and other causes.to increase the success of a steadily scaling cdd program in rwanda, partners developed and added a new coaching and facilitation component. the facilitated collective action process (fcap) provides six to nine months of intensive coaching to elected local government officials, as well as an $8,000 microgrant to fund social enterprises and subsequent projects or businesses chosen by community members.

el acuerdo de cooperación de tres años examinará el impacto del programa mlcm y la metodología hc en una zona de conflicto plagada de narcotráfico conocida como el valle de los ríos apurmac, ene y mantaro (vraem).

title.narrative: Program Design and Learning

description.narrative: Develop and conduct needs assessments, baseline studies, targeted evaluations, special studies or other information-gathering efforts specifically for the design, monitoring and evaluation of USG-funded programs. This sub-element may also include developing and disseminating best practices and lessons learned, testing demonstration and/or pilot models, or the preparation of strategic plans and other short-term programming tasks. Note: All such activities that are carried out by partners as an integral part of their monitoring and evaluation efforts for programs funded under other sub-elements should be included within those sub-elements.

title.narrative: Malawi National Integrated Drone Logistics Network

description.narrative: The USAID DIV funding will expedite the projected scaling up of Swoop Aeros existing drone logistics network, which currently operates across the districts of Nsanje, Chikwawa and Mangochi in line with Malawis Ministry of Health and Population Strategic Priorities. The network expansion will propel Swoop Aeros operations to a national scale, spanning hard-to-reach health facilities throughout the country to improve the accessibility, availability, and quality of routine and emergency health supplies. Over the next 18 months, the program will grow to serve 140 health facilities across Malawi. Swoop Aero has successfully sustained operations in Malawi for 3 years, working with some of the largest players in global health, including UNICEF, UKAID, USAID, UPS and VillageReach to improve the availability and accessibility of essential healthcare.

title.narrative: FARMER-TO-FARMER (F2F) PROGRAM
PROGRAMME D'AGRICULTEUR À AGRICULTEUR (F2F)

description.narrative: The USAID FTF-funded farmer-to-farmer (F2F) program was first authorized by the u.s. congress in 1985 to provide for the transfer of knowledge and expertise of u.s. agricultural producers and businesses on a voluntary basis to middle-income countries and emerging democracies. the F2Fprogram was designed to provide technical services to enhance sustainable economic development, offer opportunities for knowledge exchange, and broaden the participation of the rural poor in established commodity value chains as producers and service providers. the proposed enabling farmers for agricultural transformation (EFAT) activity is consistent with the overall goals of the F2F program, with the goal of increasing rural productivity and resilience. efat is designed as an extension-focused centrally-funded award with options for mission buy-in. the activity leverages the advisory service expertise and the geographic reach of the farmer-to-farmer (F2F) program through an associate award to one of the leader with associates holders.

Le programme d’agriculteur à agriculteur (F2F) financé par l’USAID FTF a été autorisé pour la première fois par les États-Unis. congrès en 1985 pour assurer le transfert des connaissances et de l'expertise des États-Unis. des producteurs et des entreprises agricoles sur une base volontaire aux pays à revenu intermédiaire et aux démocraties émergentes. le programme F2F a été conçu pour fournir des services techniques visant à renforcer le développement économique durable, à offrir des opportunités d'échange de connaissances et à élargir la participation des ruraux pauvres aux chaînes de valeur de produits établies en tant que producteurs et prestataires de services. l'activité proposée permettant aux agriculteurs de transformer l'agriculture (EFAT) est cohérente avec les objectifs généraux du programme F2F, dans le but d'augmenter la productivité et la résilience rurales. efat est conçu comme une récompense financée de manière centralisée et axée sur la vulgarisation, avec des options d'adhésion à la mission. l'activité tire parti de l'expertise en matière de services de conseil et de la portée géographique du programme d'agriculteur à agriculteur (F2F) grâce à un prix d'associé décerné à l'un des leaders titulaires d'associés.

title.narrative: TransformDigital Spaces

description.narrative: TheTransformDigital Spaces (Transform) activity is designed to reflect feminist democratic principles (transform) activity is designed to implement a global approach to addressing technology facilitated gender-based violence (tfgbv). this activity will look at a variety of subsets impacted by this form of violence, including towards women in politics and public life. the activity will pilot practical approaches to preventing, mitigating, and responding to tfgbv in a set of countries with diverse development contexts, including internet penetration, language, religion, regional and language diversity, and will then analyze, synthesize, and share learning from the pilot activities with a broader community of practice working to address tfgbv. the pilot initiatives will aim to increase resourcing and capacity for programs and organizations implementing digital democracy and/or tfgbv activities and will serve two mutually reinforcing goals: (1) mitigation, prevention, and response to tfgbv, including towards women in politics and public life, at the country level, and (2) gaining practical, comparative knowledge into what types of programming are effective to inform global efforts to combat this problem.

title.narrative: DRG: PIDR Global Labor Program - New Frontiers in Advancing Labor Rights (GLP-NFALR)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Development, Democracy, and Innovation (D): The Global Labor Program - New Frontiers in Advancing Labor Rights (GLP-NFALR) advances labor rights and builds the capacity of worker organizations, which are key civil society actors. GLP-NFALR supports governance, rule of law, economic growth, human rights, counter trafficking in persons, disability inclusion, and gender equality objectives by increasing decent work worldwide. GLP-NFALR is managed out of the DRG Center in close coordination with activity managers at USAID Missions. GLP-NFALR will deepen USAID's engagement with local labor actors to address both traditional and emerging issues in the labor sector globally, such as migration, informal work, forced labor, climate change, inclusion, and closing civic space. The activity supports U.S. national security and trade priorities and advances a foreign policy for the American middle class by addressing abusive labor practices overseas that undermine the competitiveness of U.S. workers, and by supporting U.S. trade priorities to monitor and enforce worker rights provisions of trade agreements and global supply chain standards. GLP-NFALR is implemented by the Solidarity Center. GLP-NFALR directly contributes to the Multilateral Partnership for Organizing, Worker Empowerment, and Rights (M-POWER) initiative, which is a key deliverable of the Presidential Initiative for Democratic Renewal (PIDR) that USAID collaborates on with the Department of Labor and U.S. Department of State's Bureau for Democracy, Rights, and Labor (DRL). FY 2022 resources will be used to support GLP-NFALR programming in approximately 30 countries spanning five regions, using worker-centric implementation modalities including research, organizing, collective bargaining, communications support, legal defense and support, trade union strengthening and strategic planning, inclusive leadership development, strategic networking, stakeholder engagement and advocacy, and resiliency cap

title.narrative: Teaching and Learning for Education Excellence in the Middle East (TALEEM)

description.narrative: (USAID Middle East Regional (MER)): Through the Teaching and Learning for Education Excellence in the Middle East (TALEEM) contract, USAID seeks to conduct a variety of multi-country research, training and analytical support activities to advance student learning and success in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). This activity will fulfill three key objectives: a) produce on-demand analyses for education strategic and programmatic development and policy reform for USAID Missions; b) test emerging, cost-effective solutions for achievement of student learning with potential to scale; and c) train USAID and education sector staff on new and emerging priorities. This activity will enable the ME Bureau to: utilize research and evidence to guide education investments in the region; support timely research, assessments, and generation of evidence; test innovative solutions for learning at scale; and support USAID's MENA Missions to achieve their strategic goals and ultimately, to aid host country governments to deliver on their commitments of education for all..This mechanism will program $2,265,000 towards the Basic Education earmark and $1,000,000 towards Basic Education for Girls in Conflict.

title.narrative: USAIDs Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene Finance 2 (WASH-FIN 2)

description.narrative: washfin 2s key objectives include: strengthening governance focuses on working through government, civil society, and service providers to strengthen governance and increase public funding for the water and sanitation sector. through a collaborative and datadriven approach that aligns with existing strategies and programs, usaid will assist integrating water and sanitation into national adaptation plans and nationally determined contributions and pursue water and sanitation investments with nationally accredited entities. improving climate resilient performance of service providers provides on-demand technical assistance to increase the reliability, sustainability, and profitability of service providers, including identifying adaptation strategies and pursuing climate resilient design and linking these planned investments with viable climate and other financing options. mobilizing finance provides project preparation and transaction advisory services for public and private finance. the program also includes options for catalytic grant funding, de-risking, and yield enhancements to attract additional financial partners. advancing global learning and partnerships focuses on improved coordination and knowledge sharing across the sector. wash-fin 2 occupies an important place in the usaid global research and learning agenda and the outcomes of each country-level engagement will be promoted in global forums and through online publications.

title.narrative: Advancing Capacity for the Environment (ACE)
Fomento de la capacidad para el medio ambiente (ACE)

description.narrative: (USAID Africa Regional): The Advancing Capacity for the Environment (ACE) Activity supports USAID's work in climate change, environment, energy, and infrastructure. ACE enhances USAID's effectiveness in these areas through activities supporting communications, training, knowledge management, and facilitation/organizational development, leading to global positive and sustainable development outcomes. Using FY 2022 funds, USAID Africa Regional will support training for sub-Saharan African Missions and their implementing partners on the revised Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use (AFOLU) tool. This training will strengthen reporting of estimates of greenhouse emissions reduced, sequestered, and/or avoided from project activities by sub-Saharan African Missions and their implementing partners and will inform and strengthen the Agency's ability to design and implement programs and activities that promote sustainable land use management. $200,000 of FY 2022 funds for this IM contributes to USAID Africa Regional's Sustainable Landscapes directive of $3,000,000.

(USAID Regional África): La Actividad de Promoción de la Capacidad para el Medio Ambiente (ACE) apoya el trabajo de USAID en cambio climático, medio ambiente, energía e infraestructura. ACE mejora la eficacia de USAID en estas áreas a través de actividades que apoyan las comunicaciones, la capacitación, la gestión del conocimiento y la facilitación/desarrollo organizacional, lo que conduce a resultados de desarrollo globales positivos y sostenibles. Utilizando fondos del año fiscal 2022, USAID África Regional apoyará la capacitación para las Misiones de África Subsahariana y sus socios implementadores sobre la herramienta revisada de Agricultura, Silvicultura y Otros Usos de la Tierra (AFOLU). Esta capacitación fortalecerá la presentación de informes sobre estimaciones de emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero reducidas, secuestradas y/o evitadas de las actividades del proyecto por parte de las Misiones del África Subsahariana y sus socios implementadores e informará y fortalecerá la capacidad de la Agencia para diseñar e implementar programas y actividades que promuevan la gestión sostenible del uso de la tierra. $200,000 de los fondos del año fiscal 2022 para este IM contribuyen a la directiva de Paisajes Sostenibles de USAID África Regional de $3,000,000.

description.narrative: Under the PMVC contract, Abt and its partners will work with country governments to integrate indoor residual spray campaigns with distribution of insecticide treated nets--two proven, life-saving malaria vector control interventionsas well as new tools adopted by PMI such as larval source management.

title.narrative: Analytics for Advancing the Financial Sustainability of the HIV/AIDS Response (AFS)

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): The cross bureau funding will provide technical assistance to understand and utilize resource alignment data to maximize transparency, accountability and value of all available resources. Lead costing activities, including activity-based costing and management (ABC/M), to better understand cost drivers and improve efficiency and effectiveness of resources. Facilitate the development of analytic tools to apply health and HIV financing data for planning and decision-making. Perform private sector landscaping and analytics to advance private sector engagement and financing. Apply multiple data streams--including financing, program, and macroeconomic data--to perform integrated analytics to inform the development of sustainability roadmaps. Assist in applying the methodologies developed and utilized under PEPFAR, e.g., resource alignment or ABC/M, to other health areas.

title.narrative: Localize Global Health Security LGHS
Localiser la sécurité sanitaire mondiale LGHS
Localiser la sécurité sanitaire mondiale LGHS

description.narrative: New and re-emerging diseases spread quickly across the globe, resulting in outbreaks that overwhelm health systems and upend lives and economies. The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) prioritizes global health security (GHS) and is placing renewed emphasis on local organizations as key to the long-term sustainability of its development work and to preventing, detecting, and responding to infectious disease threats. As part of these efforts, the Localize Global Health Security (LGHS) project helps local health actors access resources and strengthen their capacity to identify and respond to pandemic threats. Through this work, we build more resilient health systems, improve health security, and save lives.

Les maladies nouvelles et réémergentes se propagent rapidement à travers le monde, entraînant des épidémies qui submergent les systèmes de santé et bouleversent des vies et des économies. L’Agence des États-Unis pour le développement international (USAID) donne la priorité à la sécurité sanitaire mondiale (GHS) et accorde une importance renouvelée aux organisations locales comme étant essentielles à la durabilité à long terme de son travail de développement et à la prévention, à la détection et à la réponse aux menaces de maladies infectieuses. Dans le cadre de ces efforts, le projet Localize Global Health Security (LGHS) aide les acteurs locaux de la santé à accéder aux ressources et à renforcer leur capacité à identifier et à répondre aux menaces de pandémie. Grâce à ce travail, nous construisons des systèmes de santé plus résilients, améliorons la sécurité sanitaire et sauvons des vies.

title.narrative: Global Health Supply Chain Next Gen Control Tower
Tour de contrôle de nouvelle génération de la chaîne d’approvisionnement mondiale en santé

Torre de controle de próxima geração da cadeia de suprimentos de saúde global

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): .The Control Tower provides a holistic commercial off the shelf (COTS) solution which combines technical, data analytics, change management, and supply chain expertise. The CT is responsible for data flows ranging from storing supply plan data and order processing to predictive analysis and dashboard development-all in support of greater end-to-end visibility, better decision making, and effective oversight of USAID Next Gen Supply Chain programs..The contractor will achieve the objectives of the Next Gen Control tower by providing an existing COTs solution with a pre-existing network of suppliers and relevant data, as well as proven experience in global health. The solution provides an open modular architecture that can evolve as the world and Next Gen technology matures. Finally, the solution achieves the Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirement with standard out-of-the-box features. These include: Security and Access Management, Application Modules and Services, Partner Data Integration, Data Management: AI/ML and Insight Engine, Infrastructure Monitoring and Security. This award is co-funded and comanaged by OHA, PMI, FP and MCHN...

(USAID Global Health (GH)) : .La Control Tower fournit une solution commerciale standard (COTS) holistique qui combine l'expertise technique, l'analyse des données, la gestion du changement et la chaîne d'approvisionnement. Le CT est responsable des flux de données allant du stockage des données du plan d'approvisionnement et du traitement des commandes à l'analyse prédictive et au développement de tableaux de bord, le tout pour soutenir une plus grande visibilité de bout en bout, une meilleure prise de décision et une surveillance efficace des programmes de chaîne d'approvisionnement Next Gen de l'USAID. La solution fournit une architecture modulaire ouverte qui peut évoluer à mesure que le monde et la technologie Next Gen évoluent. Enfin, la solution répond aux exigences PWS (Performance Work Statement) avec des fonctionnalités standard prêtes à l'emploi. Ceux-ci incluent : la gestion de la sécurité et des accès, les modules et services d'application, l'intégration des données des partenaires, la gestion des données : AI/ML et Insight Engine, la surveillance et la sécurité de l'infrastructure. Ce prix est cofinancé et cogéré par OHA, PMI, FP et MCHN...

La solution fournit une architecture modulaire ouverte qui peut évoluer à mesure que le monde et la technologie Next Gen évoluent. Enfin, la solution répond aux exigences PWS (Performance Work Statement) avec des fonctionnalités standard prêtes à l'emploi. Ceux-ci incluent : la gestion de la sécurité et des accès, les modules et services d'application, l'intégration des données des partenaires, la gestion des données : AI/ML et Insight Engine, la surveillance et la sécurité de l'infrastructure. Ce prix est cofinancé et cogéré par OHA, PMI, FP et MCHN...
